headline: OpenAI published 722 manuscripts of mathematics results from an unreleased AI model, saying they solve hundreds of open questions.
score_reason: Large release, but the solutions are OpenAI's own claims and mathematicians have not yet checked them; one point off a headline that says 'breakthroughs'.
importance_line: Mathematicians and journals now face hundreds of AI-written papers to check, and the release tests whether OpenAI follows the disclosure guidelines of a new independent advisory group, while the correctness of the results is still unconfirmed.
summary: The Verge reports that OpenAI released 722 manuscripts, grouped into 372 families of related results, from an unreleased AI model; the independent Advisory Group on Mathematics and AI (AGMAI) says they include solutions to “hundreds” of open questions. This follows the AI maths story we carried on 6 Oct 2026: today's news is the full batch, published on GitHub, with OpenAI saying the average result took about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking.
